cards.title: The Nature of the Chemical Bond (3rd ed.) — Linus Pauling (Cornell University Press)
cards.locator: Pauling, L. (1960). The Nature of the Chemical Bond and the Structure of Molecules and Crystals. Cornell University Press, Ithaca, NY.
supports: Valence bond formulation of sp, sp2, and sp3 directed hybrid orbitals.
Resonance theory in amides: partial double bond character of C-N and coplanar stabilization.
Hybridisation as an approximate mathematical wave-mechanical construction rather than a physical observable.

cards.title: The Amide Resonance Problem — Kenneth B. Wiberg (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1992, 114, 831–837)
supports: Physical origin of amide planarity and rotational barrier (approx 75–85 kJ/mol in formamide).
Distinction between pi delocalisation stabilization and sigma framework electrostatic interactions upon twisting.
Rotational energy surface: loss of p-orbital overlap upon 90-degree twist without breaking sigma connectivity.

cards.title: Modern Physical Organic Chemistry — Eric V. Anslyn & Dennis A. Dougherty (University Science Books, 2006)
cards.locator: Anslyn, E. V., & Dougherty, D. A. (2006). Modern Physical Organic Chemistry. Chapters 1 & 2.
supports: Torsional dependence of orbital overlap: S varies as cos(theta) while second-order perturbation stabilization scales as cos^2(theta).
Bent's rule: central atoms direct hybrid orbitals with more s-character toward more electropositive substituents and lone pairs.
Total conformational energy is a sum of pi delocalisation, sigma strain (Pitzer potential), and steric repulsions.

cards.title: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology (Gold Book)
supports: Hybridization definition: linear combination of atomic orbitals; explicitly notes it is a model concept, not an observable.
Radical definition: molecular entity possessing an unpaired electron (SOMO).
Allenes: hydrocarbons containing cumulated double bonds C=C=C, having orthogonal terminal planes due to perpendicular central p orbitals.

cards.title: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Unit 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure
supports: Valence bond theory, sigma and pi bond definitions, and sp/sp2/sp3 hybridization schemes.
Lone pair-bond pair repulsions in VSEPR theory explaining 107° in NH3 and 104.5° in H2O compared to 109.5° in CH4.
Boundary of introductory steric number counting.
